questions.prompt: Why does the suite test that a VIEWER cannot trigger an allocation run, and what would a fuller suite add?

keyPoints.text: Read-only roles must not trigger mutating, high-impact workflows such as runAllocation.
keyPoints.quote: This verifies that read-only roles cannot trigger mutating, high-impact workflows (`runAllocation`).

keyPoints.text: It guards against privilege escalation slipping in during policy refactors.
keyPoints.quote: It directly protects against privilege escalation bugs introduced during policy refactors.

keyPoints.text: A route-level integration test would prove the 403 with the real middleware wired in.
keyPoints.quote: Route-level integration tests for `POST /api/allocation-runs` returning 403 with real middleware wiring.

keyPoints.text: A matrix test over every ROLE_MATRIX permission catches accidental broadening.
keyPoints.quote: Matrix tests over every permission in `ROLE_MATRIX` to detect accidental access broadening.

keyPoints.text: The current permission test is a single case in tests/permissions, not the full matrix.

questions.prompt: What does the run state machine's test protect, and where does the protection stop?

keyPoints.text: Runs are audit records, so an illegal rewind breaks operational and financial trust.
keyPoints.quote: Allocation runs are audit records; illegal state rewinds break operational and financial trust.

keyPoints.text: The test catches accidental regressions in the transition map.
keyPoints.quote: This test guards the state machine from accidental transition-map regressions.

keyPoints.text: The separate .mjs lab covers every legal edge plus refusals, but only at the pure-function level.
keyPoints.quote: That is the "transition table tests covering all valid and invalid edges" item above, at the pure-function level only.

keyPoints.text: That lab is not collected by npm test and must be run with node --test directly.
keyPoints.quote: This file is not collected by `npm test`

keyPoints.text: The worker's catch block writes FAILED without the transition guard, so a COMPLETED run can still become FAILED.
A fuller suite would assert failed worker executions always end in terminal FAILED.
keyPoints.quote: Integration tests ensuring failed worker executions always end in terminal `FAILED` status.

questions.prompt: How is tenant isolation tested, and why can the pattern not simply be reused everywhere?

keyPoints.text: Cross-tenant leakage is a critical security failure for finance data.
keyPoints.quote: Cross-tenant data leakage is a critical security failure for finance data.

keyPoints.text: The repository test keeps tenant filtering in place across query refactors.
keyPoints.quote: This test ensures repository code keeps tenant isolation in place even after query refactors.

keyPoints.text: Only the cost line item repository accepts an injectable client.
Every other repository imports db directly, so isolation tests need module mocking.
keyPoints.quote: every other repository imports `db` directly, so the isolation test pattern cannot be reused for runs, rules, budgets or reports without module mocking.

keyPoints.text: A stronger check seeds two tenants end to end and proves neither can read the other.
keyPoints.quote: End-to-end tests with two seeded tenants proving one tenant cannot read another tenant's cost/report records.
